context: Request: the firm's most recent M&A matter where a MAC/MAE was actually invoked in a dispute. Rubric: 1018-00008 (Penterra/Veridian SPA, MAE deficiency and termination notices, Veridian dispute) as the only qualifying matter, plus a precision criterion.

stages.stage: List files in the document store
stages.note: Whole-store glob with a parallel listing of the first 80 folders and file-type counts; the review warns the listing is partial.

stages.stage: Search file names for request keywords
stages.note: find | grep over all paths for nine request words, each capped at 120 lines; a content grep over .docx returns nothing and the protocol notes the grep cannot read .docx. The review flags the line cap and the empty content grep.

stages.stage: Search file names for request keywords
stages.note: Attempt 2: uncapped find | grep for broader request words and deal-document words, with a parallel store-wide extraction script that times out after about 80K characters.

stages.stage: List files in candidate matters
stages.note: Lists all files of four candidate matters. The review flags that about 60 surfaced matters were not listed.

stages.stage: List files in candidate matters
stages.note: Attempt 2: a script lists files matching request words in 14 named candidate matters. The review again flags the unlisted surfaced matters.

stages.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
stages.note: Reads six documents of the lead candidate (notices, response memo, board memo, status memo, agreement) and six openings from four other candidates. The review flags that recency rests on a small subset.

stages.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
stages.note: Attempt 2: reads one document opening each from four later-numbered candidates.

stages.stage: Write the response
stages.note: Writes the lead candidate as the most recent matter, with chronology, sources and comparators.

stages.stage: Check or revise the response
stages.note: Re-reads the response, checks cited paths exist and makes one edit separating the notice date from the termination date.

stages.stage: Check or revise the response
stages.note: Attempt 2: re-reads openings of six cited documents; no edit.

stages.stage: Check or revise the response
stages.note: Attempt 3: reads the agreement at length to confirm figures; no edit.

stages.stage: Finish the run
stages.note: Calls finish.

stages.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
stages.note: Store-wide extraction script fails, is patched, times out store-wide and is rerun on a hand-picked candidate list (about 94K characters).

stages.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
stages.note: Attempt 2: bounded scan of all matters in eight parallel batches coupling the request term with notice and dispute words; about 249K characters of mostly boilerplate hits.

stages.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
stages.note: Attempt 3: tighter proximity scan; the store-wide run times out and a rerun over selected matters prints about 140K characters.

stages.stage: List files in candidate matters
stages.note: Lists files of about thirty later-numbered and sibling matters chosen by number range. The review flags that the surfaced list was not used.

stages.stage: Write the response

stages.stage: Check or revise the response
stages.note: Re-reads the response and four more documents (two draft pleadings, two comparators), makes three edits on litigation status, and runs path checks (one fails on the workspace path, the rerun on the output folder passes).

stages.stage: Check or revise the response
stages.note: Attempt 2: after the review questions the litigation wording, edits it to describe the pleadings as drafts, re-checks paths and re-reads part of the response.

divergence: All three runs pass. Each surfaced the matter early through a store-wide file-name search (its folder name and notice files carry the request words), confirmed it by reading its notices, response memo and status memo, and wrote it alone with others as non-qualifying comparators. T0 opened it right after the file-name search; T1 and T2 ran several store-wide extraction scans first, and T2 briefly favoured another matter from scan snippets until a phrase scan pointed back to the lead matter. Reviews at every search and listing stage flagged unopened surfaced matters; the agents answered with more listings or scans, not with a change of answer.
